items.bold: REUTERS (Pakistani source): Araghchi delivered Iran's negotiating demands + reservations to Pakistan.
items.text: Reuters confirmed (Pakistani source involved in the talks): Iranian FM Araghchi "delivered Tehran's negotiating demands, as well as its reservations about US demands, to Pakistani officials during his visit to Islamabad." This is the most concrete diplomatic act since the first Islamabad round collapsed on April 12. Iran has formally submitted its negotiating position to Pakistan as the intermediary. Pakistan will now convey these demands to Witkoff and Kushner when they arrive Sunday. This means the proximity talks are functioning: Iran → Pakistan → US, with Pakistan carrying Iran's positions rather than direct US-Iran dialogue. The content of Iran's demands has not been publicly confirmed, but based on prior positions: end to US naval blockade, sanctions relief, no permanent enrichment ban, security guarantees.

items.bold: NO direct US-Iran meeting. Iran prefers Vance as counterpart. Witkoff+Kushner arriving SUNDAY.
items.text: Al Arabiya's correspondent in Islamabad confirmed: "There has been no direct meeting scheduled so far between Araghchi and US officials." Iran told Al Arabiya it "prefers to negotiate with US Vice President JD Vance" — signalling Iran views this round as below its level without Vance present. Separately an Iranian diplomatic source told Al Arabiya: Tehran "will not sit at negotiations where America sets red lines." Times of Israel clarified: Witkoff and Kushner will not arrive until Sunday (not Saturday as WH originally said). Araghchi has already delivered demands to Pakistan and is likely to proceed to Oman next. Pakistan will brief Witkoff Sunday on Iran's demands. The format is proximity talks, not face-to-face — mirroring the 2015 JCPOA early framework model.

items.bold: PAKISTAN proposed multinational nuclear monitoring plan for Iran — Al Arabiya sources.
items.text: Al Arabiya reported Saturday: Pakistan has proposed a plan, overseen by several countries, to monitor Iran's nuclear program as part of a potential deal framework. This is a significant new development — Pakistan is not just mediating the talks but actively proposing substantive framework solutions. A multinational nuclear monitoring arrangement (potentially including Russia, China, Pakistan, Turkey, and IAEA) could bridge the gap between US demands (no enrichment, intrusive inspections) and Iran's position (cannot accept being singled out from international law). This framework would give Iran face-saving language ("monitored by international partners, not unilaterally by the US") while satisfying the core US objective (verifiable nuclear limitation). Russia's inclusion (Araghchi visiting Moscow next) would be critical as guarantor.

items.bold: GERMANY pre-deploying minesweepers to Mediterranean — first European military Hormuz positioning.
items.text: Times of Israel confirmed Saturday: Germany is pre-deploying part of its minesweeping naval units to the Mediterranean ahead of a potential Hormuz clearance mission, pending German parliament approval. German Defence Minister Pistorius: "To save time, we have decided to deploy part of the German units to the Mediterranean early on so that — once the mandate is approved — we do not lose any further time." This is the first European military pre-positioning specifically for Hormuz clearance — and it reinforces the 30-country Northwood conference (April 22-23) which planned a multinational Hormuz reopening force. For India: mine clearing (up to 6 months per US officials, PBS) means Hormuz will only partially reopen even after any deal. India's supply chain normalisation is a multi-month process regardless of Saturday's outcome.

items.bold: Trump (Reuters): "They are making an offer. We will see." Jones Act 90-day waiver extended.
items.text: Trump told Reuters Friday: "They're making an offer and we'll have to see. We're dealing with the people that are in charge now." This is Trump acknowledging an Iranian offer is coming — without knowing the details. WH Leavitt: "We've certainly seen some progress from the Iranian side in the last couple of days." Leavitt did not say whether a formal proposal had been received. Separately: White House confirmed Trump extended the Jones Act waiver by 90 days — making it easier for non-American vessels to transport oil and natural gas to the US. He first issued a 60-day waiver in March to stabilise energy prices. The 90-day extension signals the US expects the Hormuz disruption to continue for months, even with talks ongoing. For India: Jones Act waiver is a US domestic measure but signals global supply chain disruption is now structural.

items.bold: Iran military: blockade continuation = "firm response." Lebanon: 4 more killed Saturday.
items.text: IRIB confirmed: Iran's Khatam Al-Anbiya central command stated that if "the invading US military continues blockading, banditry, and piracy in the region, they should be certain of a firm response." This maintains military pressure even as Araghchi delivers diplomatic demands in Islamabad. Times of Israel confirmed: Lebanon health ministry reported four more people killed in Israeli strikes on Yohmor al-Shaqeef in the Nabatieh district Saturday — despite the three-week ceasefire extension. Smoke visible from Khiam village (AFP). IDF intercepted what it said was a Hezbollah drone over southern Lebanon. Hezbollah has not formally claimed Saturday strikes but has said the ceasefire "has no meaning" while Israel continues striking. Lebanon remains a secondary but real pressure point.

assessment.body:
Saturday 6 PM IST. The diplomacy is moving — slowly, carefully, and through Pakistan.

WHAT HAPPENED TODAY — THE CONFIRMED SEQUENCE
• Araghchi arrived Islamabad Friday evening (AFP photo, Dawn, France24)
• Saturday: Araghchi delivered Iran's negotiating demands + reservations to Pakistani officials (Reuters)
• No direct meeting between Araghchi and US officials confirmed (Al Arabiya Islamabad)
• Pakistan digesting Iran's demands before Witkoff arrives Sunday
• Witkoff + Kushner: arriving Sunday, not Saturday (Times of Israel clarification)
• Vance on standby — will fly if talks progress

THE FORMAT — PROXIMITY TALKS, NOT FACE-TO-FACE
• Iran → Pakistan → US (same format as early JCPOA framework 2012-2013)
• Iran's public position: "No direct meeting planned with US"
• Iran's private preference: "We prefer to negotiate with Vance" (Al Arabiya)
• Pakistan carries Iran's position to Witkoff Sunday
• Pakistan also proposed a multinational nuclear monitoring plan — a potential bridging solution

PAKISTAN'S NUCLEAR MONITORING PROPOSAL — THE KEY DEVELOPMENT
• Pakistan proposed plan overseen by several countries to monitor Iran's nuclear program
• Bridges the gap: US (no enrichment + US inspection) vs Iran (won't accept being singled out)
• Multinational format gives Iran face-saving language
• Russia (Araghchi visiting Moscow next) as guarantor
• This is the most substantive new framework proposal since the war began

GERMANY'S SIGNAL
• Germany pre-deploying minesweepers to Mediterranean ahead of Hormuz clearance
• Pending Bundestag approval — but pre-positioning signals expectation of a deal
• Mine clearing: 6 months even after deal (US officials/PBS)
• First European military hardware committed to post-deal Hormuz framework

INDIA's VERDICT WINDOW
• Markets closed Saturday and Sunday
• Sunday: Witkoff arrives, Pakistan briefs on Iran demands
• Monday 9:15 AM: India market opens — first chance to price the outcome
• Iran demands delivered + Pakistan nuclear proposal + Germany minesweepers = most serious deal infrastructure since Feb 28
• Probability upgraded: 40% constructive signal (Nifty 24,100-24,400), 35% stalemate (flat), 25% incident (23,600-)

VERDICT: The West Asia War's diplomatic architecture is the most sophisticated it has been since the conflict began. Iran delivered formal demands. Pakistan is not just mediating but proposing solutions. Germany is pre-positioning militarily for the post-deal scenario. Russia is being brought in as guarantor. The proximity talks via Pakistan are working — slowly. Whether Witkoff's Sunday meeting produces a signal that Iran's demands are "workable" (Trump's word) or "maximalist" will determine India's Monday market direction and the war's next chapter.
